Who can join?
LOADOUT is in development. RSVP opens a draft interest form; eligibility and launch details have not been published.
What happens when my project is reviewed?

Reviewers check project fit and evidence, then score Originality (what is new), Technical Depth (the hard technical work), Execution (whether it works), and Documentation (whether another builder can understand it). They assign Track XP to fields shown by your work. Accepted projects can earn Bolts.
What are Bolts and Track XP?
Bolts are global, spendable currency for prizes. Track XP cannot be spent; it raises a separate persistent level in Tools, Systems, Compute, or Hardware. Levels do not multiply the Bolts you earn.
Can my project use more than one track?
Yes. Choose tracks based on the work you do, not just the kind of product you make. Reviewers assign Track XP to the fields supported by your actual work.
Can I work with a team?
Yes. Keep your journal clear about your own contribution. Reviewers credit each person for their own approved work and assign XP to the tracks that work used.
What kinds of project work may fit?

Fit depends on the technical work, not just the product label. The examples above are possible directions, not guaranteed approvals. Using AI does not automatically rule out a project; reviewers assess what you built and can explain.
How is work tracked?

The planned tools are Hackatime for coding and Lapse for eligible hardware and other non-code work. Your journal connects tracked time to notes about what you built, why you made choices, and how you checked the result. Full tracking instructions will be published before launch.
Can I use AI while building?
Yes. Explain how you used AI and show what you understand and built yourself. AI use alone does not make a project ineligible.
What are Community Eras?

An Era is a shared technical theme that approved projects help the community move forward. Projects can follow optional objectives across the four tracks and contribute Era Points to shared progress; these are separate from personal Track XP and spendable Bolts.
What is Research Mode?

Research Mode is an optional modifier for any track. Publish a clear, reproducible technical report with your project to earn bonus Track XP and reach higher levels, which can improve your discounts in that track. It is not a fifth track; the exact bonus and review criteria will be published before launch.
How do Field Requisitions work?

A matching Requisition raises the savings cap so more of your earned track discount can apply to one eligible order. It adds no Bolts or discount rate. Each is one-use, never expires, cannot be transferred, and only one can be used per order. Minimum item values and level requirements still apply.
How do Custom Orders work?

Reviewed shipped work earns Track XP toward a relevant-track request tier. The team reviews item fit and fulfillment, then provides a final Bolt quote to accept or decline. Custom Order requests are not open yet.
How do I RSVP?
The RSVP link opens an external draft interest form. Sending interest does not enroll you or confirm eligibility.
